$comment: A retrieval evaluation set. Each case names the question and the role
asking it, then asserts one of three things:
expect_sections   at least one of these must reach the top k — recall
forbid_documents  none of these may be retrieved at all — role isolation
expect_empty      nothing at all should come back
A recall case may add `expect_documents`, which requires the section to
have come from one of the named documents. The corpus holds two service
manuals for two models of the same softener, and they have a section
called 'Resin Replacement' each. Retrieving the wrong one is an answer
with the wrong part number in it, delivered confidently — and a check on
the section name alone scores it as a hit.
The distinction between forbid_documents and expect_empty matters. A role
that cannot read the service manual may still legitimately retrieve the
warranty policy for the same question; asserting an empty result there
would be testing the wrong thing and would fail for the right reasons.
Written by hand against the synthetic corpus, which is the only honest way
to build one of these — a set generated from the same embeddings it is
